documents.title: Echo — High performance, minimalist Go web framework
documents.description: Fast, extensible, minimalist Go web framework built on net/http. Radix-tree router, request binding, centralized error handling, and a concrete Context struct in v5.
documents.searchText: # echo {#echo} is a **high performance, extensible, minimalist go web framework** built on go's standard `net/http`. it interoperates with the library through `echo.wraphandler` and `echo.wrapmiddleware`, adds parts leaves to you: fast radix-tree router, request binding pluggable validation, official third-party middleware, centralized error handling. actively maintained, `v5` current release line. requires **go 1.25 or higher** (module `go 1.25.0` at documented commit). ## what you get {#what-you-get} - **radix-tree routing** — static, parameter wildcard routes; static routes match first see [routing context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html). **middleware, before after `e.pre` runs routing, `e.use` [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html). **data binding** json, xml, form, query path parameters, validation [binding handling](/sourcey/guides/binding-error-handling.html). **centralized handling** one `httperrorhandler` for every handler middleware returns **a concrete `context`** in v5 `context` struct, not an interface, handlers take `*echo.context` [context responses](/sourcey/guides/context-responses.html). **migration from v4** breaking changes, v4 support dates [migration → v5](/sourcey/guides/migration-v4-v5.html). where start {#where-to-start} new echo? read [quickstart](/sourcey/quickstart.html) install, your "hello, world!" server, core concepts. already routing? context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html) [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html) cover daily api. shipping production? handling](/sourcey/guides/binding-error-handling.html) responses](/sourcey/guides/context-responses.html) sharp edges (binding failures, responses, response helpers). api reference {#api-reference} [go api](/sourcey/api.html) tab full `github.com/labstack/echo/v5` package, generated package source: 38 types, 55 package-level functions, 232 methods, 78 constants, 21 variables including `echo`, `context`, `config`, `router`, `group`, `routeinfo`, `defaultbinder`, `httperror`, helpers. version {#documented-version} this site documents **labstack/echo @ 59aacdd** (commit `59aacddc4a13904b8a80a76f1ec838c495b5feca`, 20 nov 2026, v5.4.7), mit licensed. source links point that exact commit github.

documents.title: Quickstart
documents.description: Install Echo v5, run your first Hello World server, and learn the core concepts — Echo instance, routes, handlers, Start.
documents.searchText: # quickstart {#quickstart} echo v5 requires **go 1.25 or higher**. if you need to install upgrade go, visit the [official go download page](https://go.dev/dl/). ## {#install} create a new directory for your project, initialize modules, then echo: ```bash mod init myapp get github.com/labstack/echo/v5 ``` hello, world! {#hello-world} ```go package main import ( "log/slog" "net/http" "github.com/labstack/echo/v5" "github.com/labstack/echo/v5/middleware" ) func main() { e := echo.new() e.use(middleware.requestlogger()) // log requests with log/slog e.use(middleware.recover()) recover from panics and return an error e.get("/", hello) err e.start(":8080"); != nil slog.error("failed start server", "error", err) } hello(c *echo.context) c.string(http.statusok, "hello, world!") run it send request: ```console $ . curl http://localhost:8080/ `e.start` shuts server down gracefully on <kbd>ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>c</kbd>. core concepts {#core-concepts} this simple introduces of - **echo instance** — `echo.new()` creates application. `echo.newwithconfig` takes `config` tune (see in [go api](/sourcey/api.html)). **routes** `e.get`, `e.post`, `e.put`, `e.delete`, friends register handlers method + path. paths support parameters (`:id`) wildcards (`*`) see [routing context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html). **handlers** handler `*echo.context` (a pointer concrete `context` struct) returns `error`. `c.string`, `c.json`, `c.html`, `c.file` write response [context responses](/sourcey/guides/context-responses.html). **middleware** `e.use` registers that after routing; `e.pre` before routing [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html). **start** `e.start(":8080")` starts server. only errors are not `http.errserverclosed`, so graceful shutdown ctrl+c is error. next steps {#next-steps} context](/sourcey/guides/routing-context.html) parameters, wildcards, groups, route info. [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html) `pre`/`use` split, requestlogger, recover. [binding handling](/sourcey/guides/binding-error-handling.html) binding request data, custom responses.

documents.title: Routing and context
documents.description: Route parameters, wildcards, route groups, the v5 Router interface, and reading route info from the context.
documents.searchText: # routing and context {#routing-and-context} echo's router is a radix tree. static routes match first, then parameter wildcard routes. ## basic {#basic-routing} ```go e := echo.new() e.get("/", func(c *echo.context) error { return c.string(http.statusok, "hello, world!") }) e.post("/users", createuser) e.put("/users/:id", updateuser) e.delete("/users/:id", deleteuser) ``` every http method has helper: `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete`, `patch`, `head`, `options`, `connect`, `trace`, plus `any` (all methods) `match` (an explicit list). `add` registers route for any string, `addroute` pre-built `route`. parameters wildcards {#parameters-and-wildcards} // get /users/42 — c.param("id") == "42" e.get("/users/:id", "user "+c.param("id")) /files/docs/guide.pdf c.param("*") "docs/guide.pdf" e.get("/files/*", "file "+c.param("*")) `c.param` reads captured value by name (`"*"` the wildcard). `c.paramor("id", "default")` returns fallback when absent, `c.path()` registered pattern (for example `/users/:id`), not concrete request path. `c.pathvalues()` all values at once. groups {#groups} share prefix middleware: api e.group("/api") api.use(middleware.jwtwithconfig(jwtconfig)) runs in group api.get("/users", listusers) /api/users api.post("/users", post admin api.group("/admin") /api/admin/... admin.get("/stats", stats) `group` supports same helpers as `echo` (`get`, nesting, `static`, `file`, `use`). middleware on only that group's files {#static-files} e.static("/assets", "public") serves ./public /assets/* e.staticfs("/assets", fs) an fs.fs e.file("/favicon.ico", "favicon.ico") since v5.4.7, `static` with without trailing slash `prefix/*` `prefix` redirect to `prefix/` so `/assetsadmin/private.txt` can no longer escape guard `/assets/admin` (ghsa-76qj-xf66-r429). prefer `group.static` over `middleware.static` attached `group.use` sit behind guards: variant protected guards inside (ghsa-5hp7-4fcm-57f9). interface (v5) {#the-router-interface-v5} v5 adds `router` implementations be swapped. `e.router` current router, `routerconfig` configures it. default `defaultrouter`, created `newdefaultrouter` or `newconcurrentrouter`. `e.routenotfound` handler requests route; it, unmatched 404 from `errnotfound`. `c.routeinfo()` matched route's info (`routeinfo`): method, path pattern, name. it reliable way log meter instead of pool {#context-pool} reuses `context` through pool: `acquirecontext` takes one, `releasecontext` handlers never need call these framework does per but custom servers built `servehttp` must hold `*context` after returns.

documents.title: Middleware
documents.description: The Pre/Use split, RequestLogger with log/slog, Recover, and the official middleware packages.
documents.searchText: # middleware {#middleware} is a function wrapping handler. echo splits it in two places: - **`e.pre`** runs **before routing**, so can rewrite the path or method. use for rewrites, trailing-slash handling, and method overrides. **`e.use`** **after around matched logging, recovery, auth, cors, everything else. ```go e := echo.new() e.pre(middleware.removetrailingslash()) e.use(middleware.requestlogger()) // log requests with log/slog e.use(middleware.recover()) recover from panics return an error e.use(middleware.cors()) cors headers ``` `e.middlewares()` returns registered `use` middleware; `e.premiddlewares()` `pre` middleware. both run registration order. ## requestlogger (v5 logging) {#requestlogger-v5-logging} v5 drops old logging interface uses standard library's `log/slog` instead. there no `middleware.logger` anymore — logger `middleware.requestlogger`: e.use(middleware.requestloggerwithconfig(middleware.requestloggerconfig{ logmethod: true, loguri: logstatus: loglatency: logremoteip: logerror: logvaluesfunc: func(c *echo.context, v middleware.requestloggervalues) { c.logger().info("request", "method", v.method, "uri", v.uri, "status", v.status) nil }, })) `requestloggerwithconfig` takes `requestloggerconfig`; no-arg `requestlogger()` defaults. handlers reach same `*slog.logger` through `c.logger()`, `c.setlogger` replaces per request. {#recover} `recover` catches converts them into passed to `httperrorhandler` (a 500 by default). register early before cannot be recovered it. official {#official-middleware} maintained team, `middleware` package of this module: | what does --- `requestlogger` / structured request `recoverwithconfig` panic recovery `cors` `corswithconfig` cross-origin resource sharing `csrf` `csrfwithconfig` csrf token protection `gzip` `gzipwithconfig` response compression (honors `accept-encoding` quality values since v5.4.7) `bodylimit` `bodylimitwithconfig` body size limit `basicauth` `basicauthwithconfig` http basic authentication `bodydump` `bodydumpwithconfig` request/response `compress` (alternative gzip) `decompress` decompression `contexttimeout` per-request context timeout jwt authentication, casbin/sessions/pprof, opentelemetry, prometheus live separate repositories: [labstack/echo-jwt](https://github.com/labstack/echo-jwt), [labstack/echo-contrib](https://github.com/labstack/echo-contrib), [labstack/echo-otel](https://github.com/labstack/echo-otel), [labstack/echo-prometheus](https://github.com/labstack/echo-prometheus). check each one version (`v4` `v5`) supports adopting writing {#writing-middleware} next handler handler: func onlyjson(next echo.handlerfunc) echo.handlerfunc *echo.context) if c.request().header.get("accept") != "application/json" echo.newhttperror(http.statusnotacceptable) } next(c) e.use(onlyjson) `echo.handlerfunc` type v5: `func(c error`. returning sends see [binding handling](/sourcey/guides/binding-error-handling.html).

documents.title: Binding and error handling
documents.description: Binding JSON, XML, form, query and path data into structs; validation; the HTTPError type and custom error handlers.
documents.searchText: # binding and error handling {#binding-and-error-handling} ## request data {#binding-request-data} `c.bind` decodes the body (json, xml, or form, by `content-type`) plus query path parameters into a struct: ```go type user struct { name string `json:"name" form:"name" query:"name"` email `json:"email" form:"email" query:"email"` } func createuser(c *echo.context) u := new(user) if err c.bind(u); != nil return echo.newhttperror(http.statusbadrequest, err.error()) // use ... c.json(http.statuscreated, u) ``` reads, in order: parameters, then body. failure returns `bindingerror` — since v5.4.7, map whose value is not `string`, `[]string`, `any` an instead of silently skipping values, named types no longer panic. fine-grained helpers bind one source each: `echo.bindbody`, `echo.bindqueryparams`, `echo.bindpathvalues`, `echo.bindheaders`. `binder` interface (implemented `defaultbinder`, default on `e.binder`) lets you replace whole step; `e.binder` field to set. validation {#validation} customvalidator validator *validator.validate (cv *customvalidator) validate(i any) cv.validator.struct(i) e.validator = &customvalidator{validator: validator.new()} set `e.validator` any implementing `validate(any) error`. `c.validate(i)` runs it; `c.validatectx(ctx, i)` it with context. without registered, `validate` `errvalidatornotregistered`. errors: httperror {#errors-httperror} handlers signal failures returning error. `httperror` carries code message: echo.errnotfound 404, predefined "name required") required", map[string]string{"field": "name"}) errors cover common codes: `errbadrequest`, `errunauthorized`, `errforbidden`, `errnotfound`, `errmethodnotallowed`, `errrequesttimeout`, `errstatusrequestentitytoolarge`, `errunsupportedmediatype`, `errtoomanyrequests`, `errinternalservererror`, `errbadgateway`, `errserviceunavailable`, `errvalidatornotregistered`, `errrenderernotregistered`, `errcookienotfound`. has `code` `message` fields; `newbindingerror` wraps failures. handler {#the-error-handler} every middleware goes place: `e.httperrorhandler`. `defaulthttperrorhandler`, which writes json (or html, `accept`) message. control format: e.httperrorhandler func(err error, c http.statusinternalservererror he, ok err.(*echo.httperror); he.code log it, write your own c.logger().error("request failed", "error", err) !c.response().committed c.json(code, map[string]any{"error": err.error()}) `problemdetailshttperrorhandler` built-in alternative that rfc 9457 problem-details responses. two details matter when writing custom handler: check `c.response().committed` before (the response may already be partially sent), remember strip `content-encoding`, `content-length`, `content-disposition` (since v5.4.7) skips step can send stale `content-length`

documents.title: Context and responses
documents.description: The v5 Context struct, request accessors, response helpers, and the generic ContextGet helpers.
documents.searchText: # context and responses {#context-and-responses} ## is a struct in v5 {#context-is-a-struct-in-v5} v4 `context` was an interface; it concrete struct, handlers take pointer to it: ```go // — no longer valid func handler(c echo.context) error { ... } *echo.context) ``` because new methods can be added minor versions without breaking existing code. the framework hands each request pooled `*context` (`acquirecontext` / `releasecontext`); do not hold onto after handler returns. reading {#reading-the-request} c.request() *http.request c.param("id") path parameter c.paramor("id", "none") with fallback c.queryparam("q") query value c.queryparamor("q", "") c.queryparams() url.values all parameters c.querystring() raw string c.formvalue("name") form c.formvalueor("name", "")// c.formvalues() values c.cookie("session") *http.cookie, or errcookienotfound c.cookies() cookies c.realip() client ip (uses e.ipextractor) c.scheme() http https e.schemeextractor) c.istls() whether tls c.iswebsocket() websocket upgrade c.path() registered route pattern, e.g. /users/:id c.routeinfo() matched info (method, path, name) `c.get(key)` `c.set(key, value)` store request-scoped values. generic helpers read them type-safely: user, ok := echo.contextget[user](c, "user") tenant echo.contextgetor(c, "tenant", "default") writing {#writing-responses} c.string(http.statusok, "hello, world!") c.json(http.statusok, map[string]string{"hello": "world"}) c.jsonpretty(http.statusok, data, " ") c.jsonp(http.statusok, "callback", data) c.xml(http.statusok, c.xmlpretty(http.statusok, c.html(http.statusok, "hi") c.htmlblob(http.statusok, []byte("hi")) c.blob(http.statusok, "application/octet-stream", c.stream(http.statusok, "text/plain", reader) c.file("/path/to/file.pdf") c.filefs("file.pdf", fs) c.attachment("/path/to/report.pdf", "report.pdf") content-disposition: attachment c.inline("/path/to/report.pdf", inline c.nocontent(http.statusnocontent) c.redirect(http.statusseeother, "/login") c.render(http.statusok, "hello.html", needs e.renderer set, else errrenderernotregistered `c.response()` returns `*response` (a wrapper around `http.responsewriter` `committed` state byte counting). since v5.4.7, `response.flush` commits uncommitted response, `writeheader` passes 1xx informational codes (such as `103 early hints`) through committing. templates {#templates} type template *template.template (t *template) render(w io.writer, name string, data any, c return t.templates.executetemplate(w, name, = &template{templates: template.must(template.parseglob("views/*.html"))} set `e.renderer` any implementing `render(io.writer, *context) error`. calling `c.render` renderer `errrenderernotregistered`.

documents.title: Migration v4 → v5
documents.description: The breaking changes from Echo v4 to v5 — Context as a struct, slog logging, the Router interface — and the v4 support dates.
documents.searchText: # migration v4 → v5 {#migration-v4--v5} echo `v5` (current release line, first released 2026-01-18; this site documents v5.4.7) is a maintenance with major breaking changes. the full list in [api_changes_v5.md](https://github.com/labstack/echo/blob/master/api_changes_v5.md) repository. changes that touch nearly every application are below. ## context: interface concrete struct {#context-interface--concrete-struct} single biggest change. `context` was an interface; it struct, and **every handler must take pointer**: ```go // func handler(c echo.context) error { return c.json(200, map[string]string{"hello": "world"}) } *echo.context) ``` middleware signatures change same way: `echo.handlerfunc` now `func(c error`, `echo.middlewarefunc` wraps that. custom types implemented no longer compile against — use directly, or wrap it. payoff: because maintainers can add methods minor versions without your code. logging: old gone, slog {#logging-the-old-interface-is-gone-slog-is-in} drops logging uses standard library's `log/slog`. `middleware.logger` gone; `middleware.requestlogger` (or `requestloggerwithconfig`) instead, reach logger from handlers `c.logger()`. see [middleware](/sourcey/guides/middleware.html). routing: router {#routing-a-router-interface} adds `router` (`e.router`, `routerconfig`, `defaultrouter`) so routing implementations be swapped. default radix-tree behavior unchanged: static routes match first, then parameters wildcards. `c.routeinfo()` new returns matched route's method, path pattern, name. generic helpers *context {#generic-helpers-take-context} (`contextget`, `contextgetor`) `*context`, form were renamed to `formvalue*` family (`formvalue`, `formvalueor`, `formvalues`). update call sites used names. test helpers: echotest {#new-test-helpers-echotest} `echotest` package for middleware. separate module, not covered by reference (root only). version support {#version-support} | bug fixes security --- 5.x yes 4.x, latest until 2026-12-31 2027-12-31 older releases upgrade 4.x routine end on 2026-12-31. free, public, security-only continue 2027-12-31, patch of version. requires go 1.26 later. start projects v5, plan upgrades `api_changes_v5.md`. checklist {#checklist} 1. signature `echo.context` `*echo.context`. 2. replace `middleware.requestlogger`; move configuration `requestloggerconfig` / 3. module path: `go get github.com/labstack/echo/v5`. 4. removed/renamed (form `formvalue*`; check `api_changes_v5.md` list). 5. re-run tests hand-rolled harnesses.
